children: developed its generative AI shopping assistant Sparky to very little fanfare as part of a broader push into what it called adaptive retail. While early buzz was light, the payoff for Walmart
investing in Sparky is just beginning.

CEO John Furner noted that in Walmart's third quarter, U.S. usage of Sparky climbed 129% year over year, with baskets associated with the assistant running 40% larger. The AI assistant helps shoppers discover items, plan meals, summarize reviews, turn photos of handwritten lists into carts, and reorder staples based on inventory positioning, pricing, and delivery speed.

began its efforts to scale generative AI across customers, members, associates, and partners in 2024. The retail giant introduced Sparky in June 2025 inside its app and web experience, pairing text chat with voice and image inputs. Rather than relying on a single bot for everything, Walmart

structured its AI ecosystem around specialized agents, separating shopping discovery in Sparky from dedicated customer-support automation that handles order lookup, returns, and delivery updates. The company also expanded beyond proprietary surfaces by partnering earlier this year with OpenAI
to bring Sparky into ChatGPT and building a Google

to help power Sparky itself using Claude models such as Claude Sonnet 4.6. On the consumer side, rather than embedding a standalone Sparky widget inside Claude, Walmart opened its Agent Gateway, built on Anthropic's
Model Context Protocol, in October. This allows approved third-party assistants, including Claude, to search Walmart's
catalog and prepare orders directly on a shopper's behalf using user-controlled Agent Profiles and spending limits.

Looking ahead, Walmart plans to scale Sparky across more markets, languages, and shopping modes while building infrastructure for third-party AI agents. It has already rolled Sparky out in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Sam's Club with support for languages such as Spanish and French. Next, Walmart

is introducing Agent Profiles so shoppers can set permissions, spending limits, track agent purchases separately, or revoke access, alongside a Walmart Agent Gateway to govern how approved external agents interact with its catalog.

title: From ChatGPT to Claude deals: Walmart looks like an agentic AI winner
